contracts: Separate explicit breditor/relay-document-suggestions V1 activation requires a writer-transport V2 room. Existing constructors remain disabled and V1 rooms are refused without migration.
Reserved host effect writer 18446744073709551614 is separate from immutable genesis writer 1 and ordinary client allocations. It never has a client lease or reserves a user's counters.

Suggestion Propose/Review rights are independently owner-granted. A Reader can propose; Review allows Reject, while Accept also requires current document Editor rights. Existing document and comment roles never implicitly confer these rights.

Immutable publication binds native source proof, authenticated creator and complete durable semantic cuts. Missing source remains client-owned Pending work. Repacked retries retain original packet bytes and sequence.

Accept privately stages the original native intent and independently admits its V2 group into an unpublished room receiver. Reject has no document effect. Both kinds finalize once through the room's serialized server order.

One append/fsync record contains the deciding principal, original request, native effect metadata and effect frame. Only then are the room receiver, host author and decision map published. Opposing retries return the ORIGINAL finalization, not the newly requested choice.

Separate owned Accept records bind an authenticated current document lease to its exact writer. Same-account retries from another device never take over that writer. Replay rechecks original account ownership/rights without requiring an expired ephemeral lease. Old unowned decisions remain unowned; the optional serialized field is omitted for those original records.
Changed original targets produce explicit Conflict and leave the proposal pending. No stale snapshot overwrite or plain-text fallback is introduced.

Recovery rechecks original permission, source intent, effect semantic start and canonical writer receipt. Invalid complete records cannot be hidden by truncating an incomplete tail. Uncertain writes fence all room reads/writes.

Accepted host-effect boundaries become accepted source cuts for future proposals and named versions. Genesis remains its original immutable seed cut. Existing disabled-room source and writer admission meanings stay unchanged.

Frozen pages contain immutable publication/decision events, not mutable proposal snapshots that leak later decisions into an older cut. Current permissions are returned separately from historical attribution.

A native combined workflow retains comments through heading acceptance, independent review Undo/Redo and named-version restore. Orphaning and later reattachment remain explicit, and complete discussion/version/decision state survives room recovery.

Empty admitted derived text blocks hash zero character identities only when the native source cut has no characters or activated flow. Real, nonempty, malformed and mismatched flows retain strict refusal. Historical container knowledge alone does not imply characters existed at the source cut.
